config.title: Running in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Where to run, when to go, and what changes during marathon week.

items.q: Where is the best place to run in Berlin as a visitor?
items.a: Start with the loop closest to your bed. From Mitte hotels, the **Tiergarten classic** (about 5 km from the Brandenburg Gate) and the **Museum Island sunrise round** (about 3 km from Hackescher Markt) are both a short walk away. Staying in Kreuzberg or Neukölln, the **Landwehrkanal towpath** and the **Tempelhofer Feld ring** are the natural choices; in Friedrichshain, the Volkspark round; by the Ringbahn in the southeast, Treptower Park and the Spree.

items.q: Can you run on Tempelhofer Feld, the old airport?
items.a: Yes, and it is one of the best flat runs in Europe: about **5 km around the old taxiway ring**, with the two runway straights for intervals. The field is fenced and opens with the daylight; **in September the gates are open from 06:00 to 20:30**. There are no taps on the open field, so bring a bottle, and expect wind, because nothing out there blocks it.

items.q: Is it safe to run in Berlin at night?
items.a: The city is generally fine for runners, but choose lit ground. **Tiergarten's inner paths are unlit**, the Landwehrkanal goes dim between bridges, and Tempelhofer Feld is closed after 20:30 in September. After dark, the lit streets of the historic centre around Museum Island and the main round of Volkspark Friedrichshain are the more sensible picks.

items.q: When is the Berlin Marathon and does it affect a normal visit?
items.a: The **BMW BERLIN-MARATHON 2026 runs on Sunday 27 September**, with the GENERALI 5K on Saturday 26 September. About 55,000 runners take part, central roads close for the weekend, and buses reroute while trains keep running. If you visit that weekend without racing, plan museum-quarter walking early and cross the course at S-Bahn or U-Bahn stations instead of on foot at street level.

items.q: Do runners need to carry anything special in Berlin?
items.a: Very little. Berlin tap water is drinkable and public **drinking fountains cluster in the centre**, but they thin out in the parks, so carry a small bottle for Tempelhofer Feld and the longer Tiergarten round. A transport ticket or the BVG app is worth having: every loop here starts and ends next to an S-Bahn, U-Bahn or tram stop, so you can always ride home if the run dies.
